@graph.name: Cambridge, Massachusetts
@graph.description: Cambridge is a thriving city across the Charles River from Boston, renowned for its world-class universities, innovative tech scene, and rich cultural diversity. Home to Harvard University and MIT, Cambridge offers exceptional schools, vibrant dining, beautiful parks, and easy access to downtown Boston.

mainEntity.name: Is Cambridge, MA a good place to live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Cambridge consistently ranks as one of the best places to live in Massachusetts. It offers world-class universities, innovative job opportunities (especially in tech and biotech), excellent schools, diverse dining and culture, beautiful parks, and easy access to Boston. The community is progressive, educated, and welcoming.

mainEntity.name: What is the cost of living in Cambridge, MA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cambridge has a higher cost of living compared to the national average, primarily due to housing costs. The median home price is around $1.25 million. However, many residents find the investment worthwhile given the exceptional schools, job opportunities, transit access, and quality of life.

mainEntity.name: What are the best neighborhoods in Cambridge for families?

acceptedAnswer.text: Popular family-friendly neighborhoods include Huron Village (quiet, great schools), West Cambridge (spacious homes, family-oriented), Mid-Cambridge (tree-lined streets, parks), and Cambridgeport (diverse community, walkable). All Cambridge neighborhoods have access to excellent public schools and recreational facilities.

mainEntity.name: How is the commute from Cambridge to Boston?

acceptedAnswer.text: The commute is excellent! The MBTA Red Line runs through Cambridge with six stations (Alewife, Davis, Porter, Harvard, Central, Kendall/MIT), providing 15-20 minute rides to downtown Boston. Many residents also bike or walk across the bridges.

Yes, Cambridge Public Schools are highly regarded. The district offers diverse educational approaches including traditional, Montessori, and innovative programs. Schools like Cambridgeport School and Tobin Montessori consistently receive high ratings.

Cambridge is world-famous for Harvard University and MIT, making it a global center for education and innovation. It's known for its tech and biotech industries, vibrant cultural scene, diverse dining, progressive politics, and historic architecture.

Absolutely! Cambridge has a Walk Score of 89 (Very Walkable) and a Bike Score of 82 (Very Bikeable). Most errands can be accomplished on foot, with grocery stores, restaurants, shops, and transit all within walking distance in most neighborhoods.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Cambridge and Boston?

acceptedAnswer.text: While adjacent to each other, Cambridge and Boston are separate cities. Cambridge is generally more residential and academic, home to Harvard and MIT, with a slightly younger demographic and progressive culture. Cambridge offers excellent access to Boston while maintaining its own distinct community identity.
